newsitem.title: USA: NeoPharm says research agreement extended.
newsitem.headline: NeoPharm says research agreement extended.

text.p: NeoPharm Inc said the National Cancer Institute extended for two years a research and development agreement with the company for exclusive rights to develop and commercialize its two primary drugs, BUdR, or Broxuridine, and IUdR, or Idoxuridine.
The extended agreement will expire on September 13, 1998, the company said. It began in 1993.

The agreement gives NeoPharm exclusive access to data from clinical trials sponsored by the institute to allow the company to obtain regulatory approval of BUdR and IUdR for use as diagnostic and therapeutic agents to treat cancer.
NeoPharm said it is preparing to file new drug applications with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for BUdR as a treatment for brain cancer and as a diagnostic aid in breast cancer.

Both BUdR and IUdR are drugs known as radiosensitizers, which improve the effectiveness of radiation therapy in the treatment of cancers, NeoPharm said. The drugs are incorporated into the DNA of tumor cells, which they weaken, thereby improving the kill rate of radiation therapy, the company said.
